card: Kernel applications deadlock if their log callback logs or destroys kernel objects, a scenario regularly triggered when garbage-collected language bindings invoke object finalizers inside a callback. This PR switches kernel log delivery to btcsignals so callbacks run without holding the logger mutex, and converts btcsignals to StdMutex to prevent lock-debugging recursion. It fixes hangs experienced in downstream bindings without needing to restrict applications to a single logging connection as attempted in #34775.
evidence: Description notes that a kernel application whose log callback logs or destroys a kernel object hangs, citing real-world reproduction in Python bindings where GC finalizers trigger during callbacks (PR #34775, PR #34374)
PR description notes new test_kernel test cases hang without this fix
problem: Applications using libbitcoinkernel hang if their log callback emits a log message or destroys an object that logs (such as a chainstate manager during language-binding garbage collection). The kernel executes callbacks while holding the logger's mutex, causing re-entrant deadlocks on the same thread.

risk.why: A mistake in callback signal dispatching or thread synchronization could cause race conditions or crashes in external applications consuming libbitcoinkernel log callbacks.

scope_notes: Changes concurrency semantics for external consumers: log callbacks will no longer be serialized and may execute concurrently across threads.
summary: Dispatches libbitcoinkernel log callbacks via `btcsignals::signal` instead of custom internal dispatching so callbacks run without holding the logger's mutex. Additionally switches `btcsignals` internal mutex from `Mutex` to `StdMutex` to prevent re-entrant deadlocks when lock-debugging features attempt to log.
